**Verdict: PASS** on DG5 round 2. The frozen candidate is `sha256:55a411ae…a3c24ce` (2207 files) at source commit `660f40c`.

HEAD is the freeze commit `7a02e7d`, not the source. The commits after the source change only `docs/delivery`. I recomputed the same candidate ID on the repository and on a complete clone. The product code is the same as `5a7c189`, plus the 14 files of the round-1 repair (T-DG5-BE-RG3).

**What I ran (all on a throwaway clone, now deleted):**
- **Gate validators:** the four historical checks (DG4, DG3, DG2, DG1) and `--register DG5` all pass. The clone builds.
- **Integration tests:** two batches covering the 78 DG5 requirements, 56 files and 586 tests, all passed.
- **Acceptance e2e in both languages:** 10/10 on the demo-initialized stack and 22/22 on the production-initialized stack, with no failure, skip, retry or timeout.
- **Text scans and scoring tests:** 222 tests passed. They find no claim of official PMI status or certification, and no DG0–DG7 text in the UI or exports.
- **My own EN and AR UI probes** on fresh stacks, with screenshots: 12/12 on production and 6/6 on the demo.
  - My first EN run had two soft failures, both caused by my probe. One was a request body in the wrong shape; the other expected 403 where the API answers 404, which is also a refusal. I fixed both and the re-run passed.
  - The background job that chained the second EN run and the AR run reported exit 1. Both runs' own logs end with exit 0 and every test passed; I couldn't find the cause, and it's disclosed in the record.

**Source fidelity and operating logic:**
- B0004, B0016, B0124, B0136–B0141, B0145, B0147, B0150 and B0152 appear verbatim. Every PMI phrase in the UI is a disclaimer.
- The Playbook Studio publish refuses weights totalling 95 % (422). 30/20/20/15/15 and the new Feasibility rubric went through draft, preview, review and publish in the UI, in both languages, and reach only new transformations. A published version can't be edited (409).
- Human-only automation actions are refused, while a valid `create_task` rule is accepted (201).
- Forecast and submitted values are labelled provisional, never validated.
- The demo shows its labels on every screen, the three roaming traceability chains, and all twelve walkthrough steps.
- I accept D-163(a), D-164(a)–(k), D-165's observations, D-166 Rules A and B, D-167 and D-168. I also judged every partial-coverage note in the register acceptable, and my own UI run closes the one for REQ-PB-093 (30/20/20/15/15 driven end to end in the browser).

**New findings (Low, not mandatory, not blocking; owner frontend-ux-engineer):**

| ID | Severity | Requirement | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG5-120 | Low | REQ-PB-093 | On the English page, the Studio "Elements" table shows the five scoring-weight labels in Arabic. The seeded rows have no English `labelEn`, so the label helper falls back to the Arabic one. |
| F-DG5-121 | Low | REQ-S06-007 | On the scoring-defaults version page, "Change in this version" says "Changed" for weights whose value didn't change, and the rubric diff shows raw JSON. The diff itself is correct. |

**Covered by tests rather than a staged run:** no test generates an executive-pack PDF containing a pending benefit value (REQ-S13-008). The pack uses the same provisional-label rules, which are unit-tested, so I accept it; an explicit test would be worth adding at DG6.

The environmental residuals (live registry, live CI, real demo identity provider, AI and notification adapters) are recorded as PASS on their offline/config surface, as the assignment instructed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG5/round-2/domain-reviewer.json` (validates against the review schema)
- `reviews/DG5/round-2/domain-reviewer.findings.json`
- `test-evidence/DG5/domain/round-2/` (logs, probe specs, EN/AR screenshots)
